title: withdrawals
description: sources/withdrawals.yaml - every product that left the corpus with no successor to alias onto. A rename is carried by an `aliases` entry on the product that replaced it; a withdrawal has nothing to point at, so the acknowledgement lives here instead. One entry is a person's ruling that a slug may stop being served, and the record of what was removed once the product and score files are gone. Normative prose, including what makes a withdrawal the right call rather than a rename or a re-score, is docs/reference/identity.md under 'Withdrawal: a product that ends with no successor'.

slug.description: The slug that left sources/products/. It stays reserved: reusing it would serve a different product at a URL a reader last saw this one on.

type.description: The product type the record carried, kept so the withdrawal can be read without git archaeology.

organization.description: The org slug that owned it. If the withdrawal empties that org's roster, the org file goes too, and is named in removed_files.

decided_in.description: The issue or pull request carrying the person's ruling. A withdrawal is never mechanical.

alias.description: Always null, and required rather than omitted. A withdrawal with an alias target is a rename, and belongs in the replacing product's `aliases` array instead. Making the field explicit is what stops the two being confused.

alias_reason.description: Why no redirect is the honest answer here - what a reader holding an old link would be told if one existed, and why that would be wrong.

reason.description: Why the product left the map, in terms a reader who never saw it can follow.

last_scores.description: The final published scores, so a later reader can see what the map used to say without reconstructing the deleted score file.

evidence.description: What established that the product is ending. Same burden as any other claim on the map: a withdrawal removes a record, so it needs evidence at least as good as the one that created it.

removed_files.description: The files this withdrawal deleted, so the git commit that removed them can be found from the record rather than from a date.
